## Heads-up before the code (one real conflict in the brief)

Your task says "Use ACK S3 CRDs (`s3.aws.upbound.io`)" — those are two different things:

| API group | Project | Bucket kind |
|---|---|---|
| `s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1` | **ACK** (AWS Controllers for Kubernetes) | `Bucket` |
| `s3.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1` | **Crossplane** provider-aws (Upbound) | `Bucket` + separate `BucketVersioning`, `BucketServerSideEncryptionConfiguration`, `BucketPublicAccessBlock` |

The stack is declared as ACK, so I've written everything against **`s3.services.k8s.aws`**. That also matters materially: in ACK, versioning/encryption/public-access-block are *inline fields on one `Bucket`*; in Crossplane they're *four separate managed resources*. If you actually run Upbound provider-aws, say so and I'll split the manifests — the overlay/patch structure stays the same either way.

Second note: **nothing in this feature is secret.** Bucket names, ARNs and OIDC issuer URLs are not sensitive, so I have not added a SOPS-encrypted file. Adding an encrypted secret containing only an account ID would be cargo-culting. The account-specific values are wired via overlay patches instead. If you want them out of Git for tenancy reasons, the right lever is a `ConfigMap` produced by your bootstrap plus `postBuild.substituteFrom` on the Flux Kustomization — I show that at the end as an option.

---

## Layout

```
infra/
  s3/
    logs/
      base/
        bucket.yaml
        kustomization.yaml
  iam/
    logs/
      base/
        policy.yaml
        role.yaml
        serviceaccount.yaml
        kustomization.yaml
overlays/
  dev/
    logs/
      kustomization.yaml
      bucket-name.yaml
      role-trust.yaml
  prod/
    logs/
      kustomization.yaml
      bucket-name.yaml
      role-trust.yaml
flux/
  kustomizations.yaml   (append)
```

---

## `infra/s3/logs/base/bucket.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: myapp
    app.kubernetes.io/component: logs
spec:
  # name is overridden per-environment in the overlay
  name: myapp-logs-PLACEHOLDER

  versioning:
    status: Enabled

  encryption:
    rules:
      - applyServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
          sseAlgorithm: AES256
        bucketKeyEnabled: true

  publicAccessBlock:
    blockPublicACLs: true
    blockPublicPolicy: true
    ignorePublicACLs: true
    restrictPublicBuckets: true

  ownershipControls:
    rules:
      - objectOwnership: BucketOwnerEnforced

  tagging:
    tagSet:
      - key: app
        value: myapp
      - key: component
        value: logs
      - key: managed-by
        value: ack
```

`BucketOwnerEnforced` disables ACLs entirely — combined with the public access block that's the belt-and-braces version of "no public access". Drop it if any existing tooling writes objects with `--acl`.

## `infra/s3/logs/base/kustomization.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
resources:
  - bucket.yaml
```

---

## `infra/iam/logs/base/policy.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-rw
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-rw-PLACEHOLDER
  description: Read/write access to the myapp logs bucket
  policyDocument: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [
        {
          "Sid": "ListBucket",
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Action": [
            "s3:ListBucket",
            "s3:GetBucketLocation",
            "s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads"
          ],
          "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-PLACEHOLDER"
        },
        {
          "Sid": "ObjectRW",
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Action": [
            "s3:GetObject",
            "s3:GetObjectVersion",
            "s3:PutObject",
            "s3:DeleteObject",
            "s3:AbortMultipartUpload",
            "s3:ListMultipartUploadParts"
          ],
          "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-PLACEHOLDER/*"
        }
      ]
    }
```

No wildcard actions, and the two statements are correctly split between bucket-ARN and object-ARN resources — a very common IRSA bug is putting `s3:ListBucket` on `.../*`, which silently never matches.

## `infra/iam/logs/base/role.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-PLACEHOLDER
  description: IRSA role for myapp logs writer
  maxSessionDuration: 3600
  # assumeRolePolicyDocument is supplied per-environment (OIDC provider differs)
  assumeRolePolicyDocument: "{}"
  policyRefs:
    - from:
        name: myapp-logs-rw
```

`policyRefs` makes ACK resolve the managed `Policy` above and attach it once its ARN is populated — no hardcoded policy ARN, and ordering is handled by the controller.

## `infra/iam/logs/base/serviceaccount.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: PLACEHOLDER
```

## `infra/iam/logs/base/kustomization.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
resources:
  - policy.yaml
  - role.yaml
  - serviceaccount.yaml
```

---

## `overlays/dev/logs/kustomization.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
namespace: myapp-dev

resources:
  - ../../../infra/s3/logs/base
  - ../../../infra/iam/logs/base

patches:
  - path: bucket-name.yaml
  - path: role-trust.yaml

# Fan the env-specific names/ARNs out to every consumer, so the strings
# live in exactly one place.
replacements:
  - source:
      kind: Bucket
      name: myapp-logs
      fieldPath: spec.name
    targets:
      - select:
          kind: Policy
          name: myapp-logs-rw
        fieldPaths:
          - spec.policyDocument
        options:
          delimiter: "PLACEHOLDER"   # see note below

commonLabels:
  app.kubernetes.io/instance: myapp-dev
  env: dev
```

> Note on that `replacements` block: kustomize replacements cannot do substring substitution inside a JSON blob. Rather than pretend otherwise, **delete the `replacements:` section and just write the concrete ARNs in the overlay patch** (shown below). It's three literal strings per environment and it stays readable and greppable. I'm calling this out because a replacement-based version looks elegant in a diff and then fails to render.

Corrected `overlays/dev/logs/kustomization.yaml`:

```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
namespace: myapp-dev

resources:
  - ../../../infra/s3/logs/base
  - ../../../infra/iam/logs/base

patches:
  - path: bucket-name.yaml
  - path: role-trust.yaml

labels:
  - pairs:
      env: dev
      app.kubernetes.io/instance: myapp-dev
```

## `overlays/dev/logs/bucket-name.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-dev
```

## `overlays/dev/logs/role-trust.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-dev
  assumeRolePolicyDocument: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [
        {
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Principal": {
            "Federated": "arn:aws:iam::111111111111:oidc-provider/oidc.eks.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/id/DEV_OIDC_ID"
          },
          "Action": "sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity",
          "Condition": {
            "StringEquals": {
              "oidc.eks.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/id/DEV_OIDC_ID:sub": "system:serviceaccount:myapp-dev:myapp-logs",
              "oidc.eks.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/id/DEV_OIDC_ID:aud": "sts.amazonaws.com"
            }
          }
        }
      ]
    }
---
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-rw
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-rw-dev
  policyDocument: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [
        {
          "Sid": "ListBucket",
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Action": ["s3:ListBucket","s3:GetBucketLocation","s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads"],
          "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-dev"
        },
        {
          "Sid": "ObjectRW",
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Action": ["s3:GetObject","s3:GetObjectVersion","s3:PutObject","s3:DeleteObject","s3:AbortMultipartUpload","s3:ListMultipartUploadParts"],
          "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-dev/*"
        }
      ]
    }
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/myapp-logs-dev
```

Replace `111111111111` and `DEV_OIDC_ID` with your account ID and the EKS cluster's OIDC issuer ID (`aws eks describe-cluster --name <c> --query cluster.identity.oidc.issuer`).

**Both `:sub` and `:aud` conditions are present.** Omitting `:sub` would let *any* service account in the cluster assume the role — that's the single most common IRSA least-privilege failure.

## `overlays/prod/logs/` — same three files

`bucket-name.yaml` → `myapp-logs-prod`. `role-trust.yaml` identical but with the prod account ID, prod OIDC ID, region, `myapp-prod` namespace, and `-prod` suffixes. Prod uses the same explicitly-enumerated actions — no wildcards, per criterion 4.

For prod you may also want a retention guard, since versioning + log volume gets expensive:

```yaml
# overlays/prod/logs/lifecycle.yaml
apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs
spec:
  lifecycle:
    rules:
      - id: expire-noncurrent
        status: Enabled
        filter:
          prefix: ""
        noncurrentVersionExpiration:
          noncurrentDays: 30
        abortIncompleteMultipartUpload:
          daysAfterInitiation: 7
```

I've left this out of the applied patch list since it wasn't requested — add `- path: lifecycle.yaml` to the prod `patches:` if you want it.

---

## `flux/kustomizations.yaml` (append)

```yaml
---
apiVersion: kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
kind: Kustomization
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-dev
  namespace: flux-system
spec:
  interval: 10m
  retryInterval: 1m
  timeout: 5m
  path: ./overlays/dev/logs
  prune: true
  wait: true
  sourceRef:
    kind: GitRepository
    name: flux-system          # <-- verify against your existing source
    namespace: flux-system
  healthChecks:
    - apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
      kind: Bucket
      name: myapp-logs
      namespace: myapp-dev
    - apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
      kind: Role
      name: myapp-logs
      namespace: myapp-dev
---
apiVersion: kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
kind: Kustomization
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs-prod
  namespace: flux-system
spec:
  interval: 10m
  retryInterval: 1m
  timeout: 5m
  path: ./overlays/prod/logs
  prune: true
  wait: true
  sourceRef:
    kind: GitRepository
    name: flux-system
    namespace: flux-system
  healthChecks:
    - apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
      kind: Bucket
      name: myapp-logs
      namespace: myapp-prod
    - apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
      kind: Role
      name: myapp-logs
      namespace: myapp-prod
```

Three things I need to flag here, because I can't see the actual repo:

1. **`sourceRef.name`** — I guessed `flux-system`, the bootstrap default. Copy whatever the existing kustomizations in this file use. If it's wrong, Flux reports `Source not found` and never reconciles.
2. **No `dependsOn`** — dev and prod are separate Kustomizations with separate paths and no shared resources, so criterion 7 (independent deployability) holds. If your existing `infra/iam` kustomization creates the namespaces, add `dependsOn: [{name: infra-iam-dev}]` accordingly.
3. **`wait: true` + `healthChecks` requires the ACK CRDs to expose Ready conditions**, which they do via `status.conditions[type=ACK.ResourceSynced]`. Flux's generic health check reads `Ready`; ACK sets both. If you see health checks time out despite resources existing, drop `wait` or switch to a `CustomResourceDefinition`-aware check.

---

## Optional: get account IDs out of Git

If the literal account IDs bother you, replace them with tokens and let Flux substitute:

```yaml
# in role-trust.yaml
"Federated": "arn:aws:iam::${AWS_ACCOUNT_ID}:oidc-provider/oidc.eks.${AWS_REGION}.amazonaws.com/id/${OIDC_ID}"
```

```yaml
# in the Flux Kustomization
spec:
  postBuild:
    substituteFrom:
      - kind: ConfigMap
        name: cluster-vars       # created by bootstrap, not by Flux
```

This is the idiomatic Flux answer and is a better fit than SOPS, which is for *secrets*, not for *environment coordinates*. Trade-off: `kustomize build` locally no longer produces valid manifests, so your CI validation step needs to run `flux build kustomization` instead.

---

## Verify

```bash
kustomize build overlays/dev/logs   | kubeconform -strict -ignore-missing-schemas
kustomize build overlays/prod/logs  | kubeconform -strict -ignore-missing-schemas
diff <(kustomize build overlays/dev/logs) <(kustomize build overlays/prod/logs)
```

That last diff should show *only* names, ARNs, namespace, region and labels — if anything structural differs, an overlay has drifted from base.
